input_references.role: Timestamped GPS trajectory points linked by trajectory_id

metadata.goal: Compare mobility patterns of trajectories remaining within one urban area and those crossing between different areas of Montréal.
metadata.category: Within-area and cross-area Montréal trajectories with purpose, mode, timing, area labels, route directness, GPS positions, and point speeds.
metadata.header: MTL Trajet: 19 Within Cross Area Mobility Patterns
metadata.dataset_description: Within-area and cross-area Montréal trajectories with purpose, mode, timing, area labels, route directness, GPS positions, and point speeds.
metadata.metric_note: Distances are calculated from delivered GPS polylines; average point speed and duration are synchronized with the point table. Montréal's long island axis runs approximately southwest–northeast, so signed axis displacement summarizes the dominant travel direction.

plot.title: Purpose Mix by Area Relation
plot.description: The plot is generated from the supplied case tables.

insight_list.question: How does purpose composition differ between within-area and cross-area trips?
insight_list.insight: Within-area trips are dominated by shopping, dining, and leisure, whereas cross-area trips contain larger shares of work and education travel.

plot.title: Mode and Distance by Area Relation
plot.description: The plot is generated from the supplied case tables.

insight_list.question: How do mode composition and distance differ between within-area and cross-area trips?
insight_list.insight: Walking and cycling concentrate in short within-area movements, while public transit and motor vehicles dominate longer cross-area trajectories.

plot.title: Departure Timing by Area Relation and Purpose
plot.description: The plot is generated from the supplied case tables.

insight_list.question: When do cross-area work and education trips occur relative to within-area discretionary trips?
insight_list.insight: Cross-area work and education trips cluster around morning and evening peaks, whereas within-area discretionary travel is distributed more broadly.

plot.title: Late-night Direct Leisure Exceptions
plot.description: The plot is generated from the supplied case tables.

insight_list.question: Which cross-area discretionary trips are unusually late and direct?
insight_list.insight: A small set of cross-area leisure trips occurs late at night and follows unusually direct routes compared with other discretionary travel.

insights: Within-area trips are dominated by shopping, dining, and leisure, whereas cross-area trips contain larger shares of work and education travel.
Walking and cycling concentrate in short within-area movements, while public transit and motor vehicles dominate longer cross-area trajectories.
Cross-area work and education trips cluster around morning and evening peaks, whereas within-area discretionary travel is distributed more broadly.
A small set of cross-area leisure trips occurs late at night and follows unusually direct routes compared with other discretionary travel.
summary: Within-area travel is mainly discretionary and active, while cross-area travel is longer, more commute-oriented, and mostly motorized. Five late-night cross-area leisure trajectories form unusually direct exceptions.
evidence_policy: Claims describe patterns in this controlled constructed dataset and do not establish causal relationships.
